chunks.text: Neem (Azadirachta indica) is a fast-growing evergreen tree in the mahogany family Meliaceae, native to the Assam region, Bangladesh and Pakistan in the Indian subcontinent and to Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam in Indochina; it has since been widely introduced across the tropics and subtropics, from South America and West Africa to Indonesia. It typically reaches 15-20 metres tall with a broad crown 20-25 metres wide, pinnate leaves 20-40 cm long made up of 20-30 leaflets (distinguishing it from the closely related, twice- or thrice-pinnate chinaberry), and drooping clusters of 250-300 small, fragrant white flowers. Its olive-like fruits are 14-28 mm long. Neem tolerates drought well and grows in sub-arid to sub-humid regions with 400-1,200 mm of annual rainfall, drawing on groundwater in drier areas, and is valued for anti-desertification properties, possible carbon-dioxide sequestration and maintaining soil fertility.

chunks.source: Wikipedia — Azadirachta indica (uses and cultural significance)
chunks.text: Neem seeds contain azadirachtin, a compound identified in the 1960s as a natural insect antifeedant, growth disruptor and insecticide; ground seed powder soaked in water is sprayed on crops as a biopesticide, and neem cake left over from oil extraction is used as a fertiliser. Neem twigs have traditionally been chewed as a natural toothbrush, and neem gum is used in industry as a bulking agent and in some pharmaceutical tablet coatings. However, Wikipedia notes that clinical evidence for neem's traditional medicinal uses is insufficient, and that neem oil is toxic to small children and can cause miscarriage, infertility or low blood sugar if misused. In Hindu culture the Vaishnava saint Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was called 'Nimai,' meaning 'born under a neem tree,' and neem flowers feature in festivals such as Ugadi. Neem was also the subject of a well-known biopiracy dispute: a 1994 European Patent Office patent on a neem-based fungicide was revoked in 2005 after India successfully argued the process had already been used traditionally in the country for over 2,000 years.
